research_question: Can one held-out-subject reference record provide a deployable fixed timing/amplitude calibration that materially improves continuous 8-second ECG reconstruction on disjoint records?
purpose: Establish whether calibration guidance is a viable route before implementing a learned REM-Net calibration module.
dataset: MMECG loso_v2 validation subjects on development folds 1/5/9
output: Full-window continuous ECG, 1600 samples at 200 Hz

calibration_protocol.budget: one complete record (85 overlapping windows, approximately 42 seconds)
calibration_protocol.selection: lexicographically first record_id, fixed before metrics
calibration_protocol.query: all other record_ids from the same held-out validation subject
calibration_protocol.disjointness: calibration and query are record-disjoint; no query ECG is used to estimate calibration
calibration_protocol.inference: estimate one subject-level lag and one affine map from calibration ECG; store them; query inference consumes radar plus stored constants only

arms.lag_affine: subject-level lag followed by scale and offset

lag_search: integer samples in [-40,40] (plus/minus 200 ms), selected by calibration-record pooled PCC
metrics: query-only per-window PCC/RMSE/MAE/R2, then fold macro; full 1600 samples with edge replication after shifting
checkpoint_selection: none; frozen validation-best checkpoint; no model or checkpoint reselection

gate.required: lag_affine improves PCC on 3/3 validation subjects and mean delta PCC >= 0.15
gate.on_pass: authorise a learned calibration-conditioned REM-Net pilot
gate.on_fail: do not build a large calibration architecture; reassess the calibration signal and budget

limitations: Development-fold validation probe only, not final-test evidence.
Fold 1 has only two records, leaving one query record; uncertainty must be reported.
The calibration protocol is not zero-shot LOSO and must always be labelled calibrated subject-independent evaluation.
